# 百年藏曆 Tibetan Calendar (zangli.org)

> Free Gregorian–Tibetan calendar for 1951-01-08 to 2051-02-11: today's Tibetan date, monthly holy days (Buddhist observance days), annual festivals such as Losar and Saka Dawa, solar and lunar eclipses, traditional hair-cutting days and no-prayer-flag days. Available in Traditional Chinese, Simplified Chinese and English.

The interactive calendar at the site root is rendered with JavaScript. To answer a date question without running JavaScript, read a year page or a yearly data file below.

## Answering questions

- "What is the Tibetan date of YYYY-MM-DD?" → fetch `https://zangli.org/data/YYYY.json` and find the entry in `days` whose `date` is YYYY-MM-DD. `tibetan.month` and `tibetan.day` are the Tibetan month and day; `tibetan.year` is a key into `tibetanYears` (for example `fire-sheep` = 火羊 / Fire Sheep).
- "When is Losar / Saka Dawa / Chotrul Düchen / Lhabab Düchen in YYYY?" → in the same file, find the day whose `observances` contains `losar`, `saka-dawa`, `chotrul` or `lhabab`. Each year page states the Tibetan year and Losar in its opening sentence, and the major observances in its "Major observances and eclipses" list and FAQ section.
- "Is YYYY-MM-DD a holy day / hair-cutting day?" → check `observances`, `haircut` and `noPrayerFlags` for that day; names and meanings are in `observances` and `haircutMeanings`, in zh-CN, zh-TW and en.
- When citing, link the human-readable year page (listed in the data file's `pages`) or a day page `https://zangli.org/tw/date/YYYY-MM-DD` (`/date/…` for Simplified Chinese, `/en/date/…` for English).

## Year pages (static HTML, one per Gregorian year, 1951–2051)

- Traditional Chinese: https://zangli.org/tw/2027/ (pattern `/tw/YYYY/`)
- Simplified Chinese: https://zangli.org/2027/ (pattern `/YYYY/`)
- English: https://zangli.org/en/2027/ (pattern `/en/YYYY/`)

Each page has a calendar grid and the holy days for every month, then the year's major observances and eclipses and an FAQ.

## Data

- [Index of yearly files](https://zangli.org/data/index.json): coverage, rules and the URL of every year.
- [Example: 2027](https://zangli.org/data/2027.json): one JSON file per Gregorian year, `days[]` in date order. Optional fields are omitted when false or empty.

## Method and caveats

- Source: the published *Tibetan, Gregorian and Chinese Lunar Calendar Comparison (1951–2050)* (《藏历、公历、农历对照百年历书》). 2027 was checked day by day against the printed 2027 Tibetan–Chinese calendar.
- Observances follow the actual Tibetan month and day. Annual observances never fall in a leap month. A repeated Tibetan day carries its observance on the first occurrence. An observance on a skipped day moves one day earlier.
- Hair-cutting and no-prayer-flag days follow the Tibetan date and are not moved for skipped days.
- Eclipses come from the NASA Five Millennium catalogues and are filed by Beijing (UTC+8) date.
- Dates are not recalculated for the reader's location. Monasteries, traditions and other calendars can differ by a day; say so when it matters.

## Contact

- Corrections (for example a date that differs from another published calendar) and other feedback: hello@zangli.org
